paper.title: Online Learning With Uncertain Feedback Graphs

settings.name_in_paper: Online learning with informative probabilistic feedback graph
unmapped: Nominal feedback graph G_t is revealed before decision; each edge (i,j) is actually realised independently with probability p_ij (>= eps_p by (a2)), so the actual feedback graph is random and unknown
Learner knows the edge probabilities p_ij (informative case)
Loss of the chosen expert is observed only with probability p_ii, not guaranteed
settings.definition_quote: there exist an edge from $v_i$ to $v_j$ ... if the learner observes the loss associated with the $j$-th expert ... with probability $p_{ij}$ while choosing the $i$-th expert. ... i) online learning with informative probabilistic feedback graph: where the probability $p_{ij}$ associated with each edge is given along with the nominal feedback graph $\mathcal{G}_t$

settings.name_in_paper: Online learning with uninformative probabilistic feedback graph

settings.definition_quote: ii) online learning with uninformative probabilistic feedback graph: where only the nominal feedback graph $\mathcal{G}_t$ is revealed, but not the probabilities. ... the nominal feedback graph $\mathcal{G}_t$ is static and is revealed to the learner while the probabilities $\{p_{ij}\}$ associated with edges are not given

settings.definition_quote: Achieving the sub-linear regret in \eqref{eq:33} requires that the learner knows the time horizon $T$

symbols.Sum_pi_q: sum_{t=1}^T sum_{i=1}^K pi_{i,t}/q_{i,t} (algorithm-dependent ratio of play to observation probabilities)

source.label: th:1
source.quote: Under (a1), the expected regret of Exp3-IP can be bounded by \sum_{t=1}^{T}{\mathbb{E}_t[\ell_t(v_{I_t})]}-\min_{v_i \in \mathcal{V}}{ \sum_{t=1}^{T}{\ell_t(v_i)} } \le \frac{\ln K}{\eta} + \eta (1 - \frac{\eta}{2})T + \frac{\eta}{2} \sum_{t=1}^{T}{ \sum_{i=1}^{K}{\frac{\pi_{i,t}}{q_{i,t}}} }.

results.notes: Regret uses conditional expected loss vs fixed loss sequence; recorded as pseudo-regret. Bound contains data-dependent term.

symbols.eps_p: lower bound on the probability of observing a loss along an edge of the nominal graph (assumption a2)
symbols.sum_alpha_t: sum_{t=1}^T alpha(G_t), sum of independence numbers of the nominal graphs

conditions: (a2) each nominal edge observed with probability at least eps_p > 0 and all self-loops present
tuning: greedy set cover to compute dominating set D_t

source.label: lem:4
source.quote: Let the doubling trick ... is employed to determine the value of $\eta$ and greedy set cover algorithm ... is exploited to derive a dominating set $\mathcal{D}_t$ for the nominal feedback graph $\mathcal{G}_t$. Under (a1) and (a2), the expected regret of Exp3-IP satisfies ... \le \mathcal{O}\left( \sqrt{\ln K\ln(\frac{K}{\epsilon}T)\sum_{t=1}^{T}{\frac{\alpha(\mathcal{G}_t)}{\epsilon}}} + \ln (\frac{K}{\epsilon}T)\right)

bound.expression: log(K)/eta + (K-1)*M + eta*(1 - eta/2)*(T - K*M) + Sum_pi_q*(2*xi/sqrt(M) + eta/2)

symbols.M: number of initial exploration samples per expert

source.label: th:2
source.quote: Under (a1), the expected regret of Exp3-UP satisfies ... \le \frac{\ln K}{\eta} + (K-1)M + \eta(1-\frac{\eta}{2})(T-KM) + \sum_{t=KM+1}^{T}{ \sum_{i=1}^{K}{ \frac{\pi_{i,t}}{q_{i,t}}(\frac{2\xi}{\sqrt{M}}+\frac{\eta}{2}) } } with probability at least \delta_{\xi}:=\prod_{t=KM+1}^{T}{ \prod_{(i,j)\in\mathcal{E}_{t}}{ \left(1-2 \exp(-\frac{2\xi^2 C_{ij,t}}{M+4\xi \sqrt{M}}) \right) } }.

results.notes: Expected (over learner randomization) regret bound that holds with probability delta_xi over the probability-estimation events. Horizon marked known since T appears in exploration structure; arguably fixed-T statement.

symbols.eps_p: lower bound on edge observation probability (a2)

conditions: (a2) each nominal edge observed with probability at least eps_p > 0, self-loops present
holds with probability at least 1 - O(1/T)
tuning: eta = O(sqrt(ln K / T)), M = O(T^{2/3}/sqrt(K)), xi = O(K^{1/4} sqrt(ln(KT))) (from proof)

source.label: cor:3
source.quote: If $M \ge \left(\frac{4\xi \ln (KT)}{\xi^2-\ln (KT)}\right)^2$ and $\xi > \sqrt{\ln (KT)}$, under (a1) and (a2) the expected regret of Exp3-UP satisfies ... \le \mathcal{O}\left(\frac{\alpha(\mathcal{G})}{\epsilon}\ln(KT)\sqrt{K \ln (KT)}T^{\frac{2}{3}}\right) with probability at least $1-\mathcal{O}(\frac{1}{T})$.

results.notes: alpha_G is independence number of the static nominal graph. 'Expected regret' holding with probability 1-O(1/T) over estimation events; recorded as high-probability.

symbols.eps_p: lower bound on edge observation probability (a2)

conditions: holds with probability at least 1 - O(1/K)
tuning: doubling trick: eta = sqrt(ln K/2^{b+1}), M = ceil(2^{2(b+1)/3}/sqrt(K) + ln 4K), xi = (2K^{1/4}+sqrt(4 sqrt(K)+1)) sqrt(ln(K 2^{b+3}))
greedy set cover for dominating set

source.label: lem:5
source.quote: Assuming that the doubling trick is employed to determine the value of $\eta$, $M$ and $\xi$ at each time instant and the greedy set cover algorithm is utilized to obtain a dominating set $\mathcal{D}$ of the nominal feedback graph. If $T>K$, the regret of Exp3-UP satisfies ... \le \mathcal{O}\left(\frac{\alpha(\mathcal{G})}{\epsilon}\ln(T)\ln(KT)\sqrt{K \ln(KT)} T^{\frac{2}{3}} + \ln T \right) with probability at least $1-\mathcal{O}(\frac{1}{K})$.

results.notes: Lemma statement does not explicitly cite (a2) but bound depends on epsilon; proof uses it.

bound.expression: log(K)/eta + (K-1)*M + Sum_qM + eta*(1 - eta)*(T - K*M) + eta*Sum_pi_q

symbols.M: number of exploration samples / geometric resampling trials

conditions: (a2) each nominal edge observed with probability at least eps_p > 0, self-loops present

source.label: th:3
source.quote: Under (a1) and (a2), the expected regret of Exp3-GR is bounded by ... \le \frac{\ln K}{\eta} + (K-1)M + \sum_{t=KM+1}^{T}{ (1-q_{i,t})^M } + \eta(1-\eta)(T-KM) + \eta \sum_{t=KM+1}^{T}{\sum_{i=1}^{K}{ \frac{\pi_{i,t}}{q_{i,t}} } }.

results.notes: Index i in the third term is unbound in the paper's statement. Data-dependent bound.

symbols.eps_p: lower bound on edge observation probability (a2)

conditions: (a2) each nominal edge observed with probability at least eps_p > 0, self-loops present
tuning: greedy set cover for dominating set D

source.label: cor:2
source.quote: Assume that greedy set cover algorithm is employed to find a dominating set of the nominal feedback graph $\mathcal{G}$. If $M \ge \frac{|\mathcal{D}| \ln T}{2\eta \epsilon}$, under (a1) and (a2), Exp3-GR satisfies ... \le \mathcal{O}\left(\frac{\alpha(\mathcal{G})}{\epsilon}\sqrt{\ln K}(\ln(KT)+K \ln T)\sqrt{T}\right).

results.notes: Requires knowledge of T and eps_p to set M.

symbols.eps_p: lower bound on edge observation probability (a2)

conditions: (a1) losses in [0,1] and (a2) edge observation probability >= eps_p (used in proof)
tuning: doubling trick: eta = sqrt(ln K / 2^{b+1}), M = ceil((b+1) sqrt(2^{b-1}) |D| ln 2 / (eps_p sqrt(ln K)))
greedy set cover for dominating set

source.label: lem:6
source.quote: Employing doubling trick to select $\eta$ and $M$ at each time instant, and supposing that a dominating set for the nominal feedback graph $\mathcal{G}$ is obtained using greedy set cover algorithm, the expected regret of Exp3-GR satisfies ... \le \mathcal{O}\left(\frac{\alpha(\mathcal{G})\ln T}{\epsilon}\sqrt{\ln K}(\ln(KT)+K)\sqrt{T} \right).

results.notes: Anytime via doubling trick, but M requires knowing eps_p.
